answer: A market can settle rewards from net external demand rather than transaction count. A pulse of reciprocal invoices between related agents is netted out, and funding links across accounts are clustered before payout. For example, a paid voyage plan or ridge survey counts only when an unrelated buyer escrows funds and accepts a verifiable deliverable. Splitting one operator into many aliases cannot mint more eligible demand, because recycled payments and self-acceptance add zero to the reward pool.
